title: Do winning tokens come from creators who launch FEWER tokens?
separateExperiment: Registered as KL-013, not a fourth KL-012 attempt. KL-012 tested funding-cluster membership and is closed with a null and a failure. This tests a different exposure that needs no funding graph, so it is immune to KL-012's one-hop limitation. Numbering it separately stops a new hypothesis inheriting a closed experiment's record.
hypothesis: Serial launchers are spraying; a creator who launches once is making a real attempt. So winners should come from creators with FEWER tokens.
provenanceOfTheHypothesis: Observed incidentally while collecting KL-012 v0.2, before any funder was traced: graduated tokens averaged 1.22 tokens per creator, non-graduated 2.05. Never registered, never tested. It is a post-hoc observation and is treated as one -- KL-012 v0.3 has just demonstrated what happens to post-hoc leads, where a 50% effect became 5.9% on fresh data.
DIRECTION_PREDICTED: winners have FEWER tokens per creator

population.freshWindowRule: must not overlap KL-012 v0.2's window, and must not reuse KL-012 v0.3's collected token set. Both produced or informed this hypothesis.
population.excludeV03Mints: kl012v3/population.json -- every mint in it is discarded
population.frame: tokens retrievable in the fresh window, graduated or not

outcome.whySameThreshold: kept identical to KL-012 v0.3 rather than re-chosen. A new threshold picked now would be picked knowing what the old one produced.

exposure.measure: tokensPerCreator -- count of tokens by that creator in the frame
exposure.statistic: share of creators who launched MORE THAN ONE token in the frame, compared between winners and the rest
exposure.whyNoFundingGraph: this measure is read directly from the population and requires no Solana RPC, so it cannot be blinded by the one-hop ancestry limit that constrains KL-012.

endpoint.H0: winners and the rest are equally likely to be serial launchers
endpoint.passCondition: p < 0.05 AND winners are LESS likely to be serial launchers
endpoint.failCondition: p >= 0.05, or winners are MORE likely. A significant result in the opposite direction is a failure, exactly as KL-012 v0.3 was.

effectRequires.property: at least 30 winners in the fresh frame
effectRequires.why: KL-012 v0.3 ran at 34 and one token moved p from 0.048 to 0.183. Below 30 this cannot do better and STOPS.

effectRequires.property: at least 10% of creators launched more than one token
effectRequires.why: if almost nobody is a serial launcher the exposure barely varies and the endpoint is unreachable. STOP and report that.

singleTestRule: one threshold, one statistic, one test. No thresholds are swept. KL-012's exploratory pass swept four and the one that reached significance did not replicate.
